statement: A net of a cube is made of 6 squares joined edge to edge and cut out as one piece. To fold it into a cube, edges of its outline are taped together in pairs, one piece of tape per pair. How many pieces of tape are needed?

choices.misconception: I counted all the edges of the cube, forgetting that some of them are folds that are already joined.
I counted the fold lines inside the net instead of the edges that must be taped.
I counted the edges on the outline of the net but forgot that each piece of tape joins two of them.
I thought one piece of tape is needed for each face of the cube.

hints: Every edge of the finished cube is either a fold or a taped seam.
Count the fold lines in any net: six squares held together in one piece need a certain number of shared edges. Then compare with the number of edges a cube has.
Six squares in one piece share exactly 5 edges, which become folds. A cube has 12 edges.

solutions.reliable: Count the outline: 6 squares have 6 x 4 = 24 sides. The 5 shared edges inside the net use up 10 of these sides, leaving 14 sides on the outline. Taping joins them in pairs, so 14 / 2 = 7 pieces of tape. The transferable idea: count the same thing two ways, edges of the net and edges of the solid, and the difference tells you what is missing.
solutions.elegant: A cube has 12 edges. Five of them are already folds in the net, so the other 12 - 5 = 7 must be taped, whichever of the cube's nets you use.

whyOnTest: Nets questions are usually about which net folds; this one checks that you see a net as a cube with some edges cut.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
